comment: The rules of D3.5 and D6.9 that close two routes to a forged pointer. The `.ptr` of a span or a
string stands in three positions only, each as it stands: an argument of an `extern fn` for a
parameter whose C type is no C type that C gives back in that declaration, the argument of
`str.from_cstr`, and an operand of `==` or `!=`. No cast takes a `.ptr` (D3.5). Only
`str.from_cstr` and `rt.args_init` take `p[lo..hi]` of a raw pointer, and no source names
`rt.args_init` (D6.9). The rows cover src/fort/check.ft: pseudo_field, ptr_argument,
c_gives_back, c_gives, c_type_same, c_byte, the operands of `==` and `!=` in check_expr,
raw_span_allowed, is_args_init, check_span_expr and value_of_sym. The first stage runs the
language tests of the two rules, whose goldens pin each message and its position. The second
runs check_raw_span_test.ft, which holds the two functions in a sandbox std. The table runs in
the VM with the debug preset: pass a --runner that runs tools/vm run in one slot, as
notes/environment.md says. The md5 guard reads the product compiler. The first round of a run
in the VM can read stale (notes/testing.md 1), so run the first row again before you trust it.
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort

stages.name: the language tests of the two rules
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 4 fail/spans/007 fail/stdlib/007 fail/pointers/009 fail/ffi/011 run/pointers/004 run/pointers/014 run/stdlib/013 run/stdlib/068

stages.name: the checker suite of the two functions
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 2 check_raw_span_test

mutations.what: a `.ptr` stands in each position
a `.ptr` is legal for each parameter of an `extern fn`, a channel back too
no argument of an `extern fn` takes a `.ptr`
C gives back no argument through the result
C gives back no argument through a parameter of a callback
C gives back no argument through a `mut` level of a parameter
a function pointer that C gives gives back no argument
a result that says `own` is a channel back
an argument of the variable tail is no channel back
a `void*` equals no other pointer type
`char` and `u8` are two C types
the `mut` mark counts in a comparison of C types
fixed arrays of two lengths are one C type
a fixed array of `char` and one of `u8` are two C types
the left operand of `==` and `!=` takes no `.ptr`
the right operand of `==` and `!=` takes no `.ptr`
the argument of `str.from_cstr` takes no `.ptr`
a function named `from_cstr` of each module takes a `.ptr`
each function takes `p[lo..hi]` of a raw pointer

mutations.what: `str.from_cstr` and `rt.args_init` take no span of a raw pointer
